name: Muthuvan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Read Sakthivel 1978 Muduva Dialect (archive.org): phonology has no stress statement. T. Madhava Menon 1996 description remains unreached and might cover stress.

sources.citation: SPPEL / CIIL Mysuru, Southern Zone language pages and Bhasha Sanchika repository (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: MUTHUVAN is on the SPPEL endangered-language list (research team 'MUDUVAN - Dr. Sathyanarayan'), but no grammatical sketch, grammatical-features page or Sanchika item has been released.

sources.citation: Office of the Registrar General, India. 2023. Linguistic Survey of India - Tamil Nadu.
sources.note: Muthuvan appears only in the introductory list of tribes; no Muthuvan chapter. No LSI Kerala volume exists (Census NADA catalog checked).

sources.citation: Sakthivel, S. 1978. Muduva dialect. Annamalainagar: Annamalai University (Dept. of Linguistics). 158 pp. [data 1976-77, Shenbagathozhuvakkudi, Suryanelli, Idukki]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.2 Phonology: 19 segmental phonemes; sec. 2.1.3 'There are three suprasegmental phonemes viz. length and two junctures open and close' (p.16); allophony 2.5 conditions /u/ allophones by initial vs non-initial syllable, never by stress. No use of the words stress/accent/prominence anywhere.

tone.quote: 2.1.1. PHONEMES There are twenty two phonemes in the Muduva Dialect spoken by the Muduva tribe in the Idikki District, Kerala State of which nineteen are segmental and three are supraseg-mental. [...] 2.1.3. SUPRASEGMENTAL PHONEMES There are three suprasegmental phonemes viz. length and two junctures open and close in the Muduva Dialect 2.1.3.1. Length pakki 'bird' mala 'mountain' pa:kki 'balance' ma:la 'garland' The long vowel has been treated as a short vowel plus length.
tone.locator: ch. 2 Phonology, sec. 2.1.1 (chapter-opening page, p. 15) and sec. 2.1.3-2.1.3.1 (p. 16) of either

sources.citation: Darwin, L. 2017. Language of Muthuvan - a linguistic study. Journal of KIRTADS 1 (March 2017): 71-79. Kozhikode: KIRTADS.
sources.note: Nothing. Gives 5 vowels with phonemic length, 15 consonants, distribution and clusters, then tense/person/case morphology; no suprasegmental discussion beyond length.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13(7).
sources.note: No Muthuvan section at all (covers Muduga of Attapady, a different language).

sources.citation: Menon, T. Madhava (chief ed.) 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Article 'MUTHUVA LANGUAGE', pp. 294-295.
sources.note: Nothing. One paragraph of phonology (5 vowels, 14 consonants, r-merger, l>y with gemination after short vowel in disyllables, nk>nn), eastern/western dialect morphology, glottochronology; no stress/accent statement. This is the 'Menon 1996' source the earlier scan flagged as unreached.
